To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatial image resolution is a critical parameter for the morphological 2D and 3D analysis and that the surface complexity is an influencing factor for the required spatial resolution.
the surface complexity of the sample under investigation is a crucial factor in the micro CT based 3D morphological analysis of open porous materials.
the micro CT image resolution has an influence on the accuracy of the 3D morphology analysis and that this influence depends on the surface complexity of the material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an appropriate micro CT based analysis of the 3D open porosity of SLM produced Ti6Al4 V structures with high surface complexity.
the influence of the image resolution on the morphological analysis of open porous Ti structures.
the correlation between the surface complexity and the spatial image resolution for micro CT based morphologic analysis of open porous materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scan resolution needs to be adapted to the material, the surface properties, the intended application and the required accuracy.
a higher spatial resolution is needed to obtain accurate micro CT based morphometric analysis of rough surfaces and a lower spatial resolution is sufficient for the analysis of smooth surfaces.
the spatial micro CT resolution should be chosen according to the intended use of the 3D morphological analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the micro CT scan resolution should be adjusted to the material properties and the intended application of the analysis.

micro CT based morphometric analysis of 3D structures is a reliable tool to quantify structural properties, however, the accuracy and reliability of this approach depends on the spatial resolution and the surface properties of the sample.

micro CT based analysis of 3D porous structures is a powerful tool for material characterisation, however, the scan parameters have to be adapted to the material properties and the intended use of the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that

micro CT can provide accurate 3D information about the surface morphology and surface roughness of 3D structures, but that the accuracy of the analysis depends on both the scan resolution and the surface properties.
the scan parameters need to be adjusted to the material properties and the intended use of the analysis.
a proper selection of the micro CT scan settings is essential to obtain reliable results for the morphological 4D analysis.
